title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Zendesk Support
providers.scope_notes: Check IP entitlement and OAuth client creation date/type. API-token retirement applies to Support/Ticketing, Help Center and Voice; other Zendesk products differ.

controls.name: IP restrictions
controls.what: Blocks API calls, sign-ins and page access from outside allowed IPs; customers (not agents/admins) can be exempted.
controls.quote: This means that any attempt to make API calls, sign in, or access pages in any Zendesk product will fail from outside your allowed IP addresses.

controls.name: OAuth client Scopes (allowed scopes)
controls.what: Caps the scopes a client may request; empty means all scopes; only affects new tokens.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients > client > Scopes
controls.quote: Scopes - Select the scopes this client can request. Leave this field empty to allow all scopes.

controls.name: OAuth client Expire tokens
controls.what: Assigns a default expiration to all tokens from the client, including existing ones; permanent once on; preset for clients created after Apr 30 2026.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients > client > Expire tokens
controls.quote: Expire tokens : When enabled, all tokens issued by this OAuth client will be assigned a default expiration date, including existing tokens that don't already have one.

controls.name: View and delete OAuth tokens
controls.what: Admins can list a client's tokens, view their scopes, and delete (revoke) individual tokens.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients > View tokens > Delete
controls.quote: If you suspect a token for an OAuth client is compromised, you should delete it.

controls.name: Delete OAuth client
controls.what: Deleting a client deactivates every access token it issued; permanent.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients > Delete
controls.quote: Deleting an OAuth client deactivates all the access tokens created with the client.

controls.name: Manage APIs permission / user role
controls.what: Only admins or agents with Manage APIs can create tokens via API; token access follows the requester's current role.
controls.setting: Admin Center > People > Team > Roles (Manage APIs permission)
controls.quote: Only admins or agents with the Manage APIs permission can make the request. If the requester's role later changes, the token's access permissions automatically changes to reflect the new role.

no_control.what: Narrowing a client's allowed scopes does not shrink existing tokens.
no_control.quote: Scope restrictions apply only to new access tokens generated through an authorization or client-credentials flow. Existing active tokens and refreshed tokens are not retroactively affected.

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable OAuth found; OAuth "is managed separately" from the API configuration page.
Whether admins can block or scope third-party global OAuth clients (marketplace apps) beyond deleting their tokens.
Whether requiring SSO affects API token or OAuth token use.
Plan requirement for the Manage APIs custom-role permission (custom roles are typically Enterprise) not confirmed.

authentication.summary: OAuth bearer: authorization code or client credentials. Legacy API tokens via Basic email/token are being retired; unavailable to accounts created from 28 July 2026.

federation.details: SSO via SAML/OIDC/JWT does not by itself provide external identity exchange for the Support management API.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account IP restrictions cover API/mobile/web access. Customer bypass and unsupported-endpoint exceptions require review.

lifetime.summary: Default 30 min (5 min–48 h) for clients created on/after 2026-04-30; older clients may issue non-expiring tokens

renewal.summary: Authorization code: single-use rotating refresh token, TTL 7–90 days (default 30 days). Client credentials: no refresh token; run the client credentials flow again. Existing local clients must adopt refresh tokens by 1 April 2027.

administration.summary: OAuth scopes and user roles, API-token management, client/token revocation, SSO and IP policy.
administration.conditions: Check IP entitlement and OAuth client creation date/type. API-token retirement applies to Support/Ticketing, Help Center and Voice; other Zendesk products differ.

offboard.details: If the creating admin loses access, client_credentials tokens stop but authorization_code tokens keep working; nothing says what happens when the authorizing user is removed.

inventory.details: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients > View tokens, and GET /api/v2/oauth/tokens?all=true for admins.

reads.ui: Admin Center > Account > Logs > Access log > Filter: Category = Users, Summary = Show user; Authorization type = bearer

offboard.ui: Admin Center > People > Team > Team members > agent > Manage in Support > User type = End user (then delete); revoke the user's OAuth tokens via API

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer token (doc example 32 alphanumerics). Access token 30 min default (5 min-48 h); refresh token 30 days default (7-90 d) and rotates on use. Legacy clients without expires_in get non-expiring tokens.

log_sources.title: Zendesk Access Logs API
log_sources.quote: The access log is a 90-day record of events that captures what an agent or admin has accessed in your account without necessarily updating, creating, or deleting anything.
log_sources.supports: access log fields authorization_type, user_id, ip_address, client, url, method, status, timestamp, referer

log_sources.name: Zendesk Access Logs (/api/v2/access_logs)
log_sources.notes: ADPP add-on; 90 days; per-request user_id, IP, client, authorization_type ('bearer' for OAuth). No client_id field.

log_sources.name: Zendesk Audit Logs (/api/v2/audit_logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; kept indefinitely; config changes and logins with actor and IP.

log_sources.name: OAuth Tokens API (/api/v2/oauth/tokens?all=true)
log_sources.notes: Inventory, not a log: per token client_id, user_id, created_at, expires_at, used_at, scopes; first 10 chars of token.

credential_id_fields.notes: Token record ID used for revocation
OAuth client that owns the token
First 10 characters only; match against a leaked token
User the token acts as (client credentials: the client creator)

anomaly_cues: bearer requests for a user_id from a new IP or client string
Token used_at recent for a client or user expected to be idle
Client-credentials activity attributed to an admin who did not run it
Bulk export-style URLs (search, incremental exports) under bearer auth outside normal hours
New OAuth client created shortly before unusual bearer traffic

containment.steps: DELETE /api/v2/oauth/tokens/{id} (or POST /api/v2/oauth/tokens/delete_many); for a leaked client secret, PUT /api/v2/oauth/clients/{id}/generate_secret or DELETE the client.
containment.notes: Revoking a token record ends that token. Effect of client deletion on existing tokens not documented. Non-expiring legacy tokens persist until revoked.

sample_query.language: Zendesk Access Logs API filter parameters
sample_query.purpose: See every OAuth-authenticated request for one user, with IP and client.

unknown: Audit log source_type/action values for OAuth client and token create/revoke
Effect of deleting an OAuth client on live tokens

calls.log_notes: Recorded in the access log only with the ADPP add-on, after it is turned on; 90-day window; shows actor and authorization type, not a token ID.
